title: Expose owner session API with server-side revocation and CSRF protection
requirements: Implement POST, GET and DELETE /api/v1/admin/session from the accepted API contract, using only DB-006 owner/session tables and an explicitly injected AdminSessionRuntime. Missing runtime dependencies must fail closed with a stable 503 response.

Authenticate a pre-provisioned non-disabled owner by a versioned, self-describing hashlib.scrypt password hash with a per-password random salt and timing-safe verification. Return the same private 401 result for unknown login, disabled account, invalid password or malformed stored hash; do not add account bootstrap, registration, reset or password-change behavior.

On successful login, rotate to a cryptographically random opaque cookie token, persist only its HMAC digest, issue a distinct CSRF token, persist session metadata, and return owner_id, csrf_token and expires_at. The cookie is Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, has no Domain attribute, and raw cookie values are never logged or stored.

Enforce a runtime-injected login-attempt limiter and a runtime-injected positive session lifetime policy; no default quota, origin allowlist or production lifetime is invented. Limiter rejection returns 429 without revealing credential state.

Require trusted exact Origin, application/json and X-Requested-With: crm for login. Every session read or sign-out verifies the server-side record, expiry, revocation, owner disabled marker and matching credentials_version. Sign-out also requires trusted Origin and a timing-safe X-CSRF-Token check, then records revoked_at instead of deleting history.

Return the documented {data}/{error} envelope with Cache-Control: no-store; do not enable CORS, disclose other owner fields, add CRM commands, configure production runtime, or contact an external identity provider.

Add focused API tests and PostgreSQL integration tests in uniquely named disposable databases. Tests must migrate Alembic head there, clean up in finally, and never mutate the configured source DATABASE_URL.
acceptance: A configured synthetic runtime logs in only the provisioned owner, emits a protected cookie and digest-only session record, and GET returns the documented private session data.

Malformed, untrusted-origin, wrong-media, missing-header, invalid-password, disabled-owner, expired, revoked, credential-version-mismatched and invalid-CSRF scenarios receive safe stable errors without exposing login existence or creating an active session.
Sign-out revokes the existing server-side session and later GET cannot restore it. Focused API/integration tests, scope and whitespace checks pass.

shared_paths_approval.reason: Accepted security-sensitive vertical slice over DB-006 storage. The task deliberately uses injected policy and pre-provisioned synthetic accounts rather than creating a deployment credential flow.
